subject: Fortnightly OKR sync: reliability incident roll‑forward and QBR artifacts
messages:
From: Acme Payments Ops <ops@acme-payments.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Nebula SRE Lead <sre_lead@nebula.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent latency spike impacting billing path — need short exec note for QBR

Hi Hannah,

Wanted to flag an incident we saw last night that affected the billing pipeline for several merchants between 02:10–02:33 UTC. Our telemetry shows a ~5–7s tokenization/response latency increase for inference calls routed to the "dedicated-2" capacity; that translated to delayed invoice generation and a handful of payment retries.

We know you're preparing QBR artifacts next week — would you be able to provide a short one‑pager (executive summary + A/Cs) and any action items with owners for the reliability section? Our CRO will want to see the customer impact, remediation timeline, and SLA variance numbers so we can prep slides.

Happy to share logs — attaching a sampling of request IDs from our side.

Attachments: acme-incident-request-ids.txt (text)

Thanks,
Jill Park
Director, Production Operations
Acme Payments

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Jill Park <ops@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spike impacting billing path — need short exec note for QBR

Jill — thanks for the heads up and the request IDs. We investigated overnight and have a short exec summary and an action register attached for QBR use. High level:

- Impact: ~12 merchant accounts experienced delayed invoice generation between 02:10–02:33 UTC. No data loss; requests were retried successfully.
- Root cause: transient KV-cache eviction during a resource pressure window on dedicated-2 (mix of longer context requests + an unbalanced autoscale step). Kernel selection fallback added ~5–8s for a subset of shards.
- Mitigation (in-place): forced cache warm, adjusted autoscale policy to ignore short spikes, and rolled a hotfix to the kernel selector to avoid fallback for verified quantized models.
- Customer-facing outcome: retries completed; downstream invoices issued within 1–10 minutes after the initial delay.

Attached: postmortem-acme-payments-20260925.pdf (summary), reliability-action-register-20260925.xlsx (owners + due dates), qbr-slides-draft-0925.pptx (draft slide we can drop into your deck).

Action items (short list for exec slide):
1) Engineering — finalize kernel-selector patch and deploy to Dedicated pool (owner: Marissa; due: 2026-09-28)
2) Platform — tighten autoscale step threshold for dedicated-2 and add a short-window suppression (owner: Karthik; due: 2026-09-27)
3) Reliability — add a prefix cache-health alert that triggers at 2x baseline eviction rate (owner: Vivek; due: 2026-09-30)
4) Customer Ops — send a brief post-incident note to impacted merchants with timeline and mitigations (owner: Hannah; due: 2026-09-26)

Quick ask: Vivek/Karthik — can you each confirm the owners and ETA above? Vivek — can you add the SLA variance numbers (p99/p95 token latency delta and estimated per-token cost impact) to the action register so Jill's CRO has a single row for financial impact?

Thanks — I'll update the drive folder and drop a cleaned slide into the shared QBR deck once we have confirmations.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Jill Park <ops@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spike impacting billing path — need short exec note for QBR

Thanks Hannah — concise and helpful. A few additions:

- I'll pull p95/p99 latency delta and estimated per-token cost delta and add a summary row to the action register by EOD today (will reference SUP-4212).
- For the QBR slide, prefer a single slide with: 1) one-line incident summary, 2) customer impact (merchant count + minutes delayed), 3) root cause + remediation, 4) next steps with owners and % OKR hit risk. I updated the draft slide with a placeholder for the SLA row.

Small editorial change to actions: mark the kernel-selector patch as a "canary-out-by" target (Marissa) and include a rollback plan in the register. I added two inline notes to the attached register.

On the customer-ops note: Hannah, lean factual, no remediation promises beyond what we shipped; include a point about the permanent monitoring change (prefix cache-health alert).

Vivek
CEO, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Jill Park <ops@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent latency spike impacting billing path — need short exec note for QBR

All — confirmed.

- Autoscale threshold change scheduled for 2026-09-27; I'll attach a short runbook update referencing the dedicated-2 topology.
- Created JIRA SUP-4212 to track the kernel selector canary and rollback plan; link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4212.
- I'll own the post‑deployment validation (smoke tests + 30m observation window) and will post results to the Drive folder.

Hannah — once you send the customer-facing note I'll route it through legal (quick review) and send to Jill's team for distribution.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
